answer: To resist Sybil attacks, agents stake tokens into a bonded audit pool. Decentralized clusters, structured like an isolated grove, execute game-theoretic multi-agent auditing to continuously verify interaction graphs. When topological cut verifications detect artificial subgraphs attempting to harbor fake identities, an automated slashing protocol acts like a swift comet to burn malicious stakes. This audit mechanism imposes a superlinear attacker cost relative to forged agent nodes.
